skill.name: Set image dimensions to prevent layout shift
skill.description: Declare width and height attributes on img elements to allow browsers to calculate and reserve space before image load, preventing cumulative layout shift (CLS). The browser uses these attributes to compute aspect-ratio at HTML parse time, enabling responsive scaling while maintaining layout stability.
skill.skill_body: Add width and height attributes to img elements with known dimensions. The browser will calculate the aspect ratio from these attributes and reserve the required space during layout, preventing shifts when the image loads. Use height: auto; in CSS to allow responsive scaling while preserving the aspect ratio. ## Objective prevent layout shift by pre-calculating image space reservation ## Applicable Signals - img element without width/height attributes - layout shift detected during image load - performance audit identifies CLS issues ## Contraindications - image dimensions are truly dynamic or unknown at markup time - using CSS-only image sizing without HTML attributes - responsive images with varying aspect ratios across srcset ## Intervention Moves - Identify the image's intrinsic width and height - Add width and height attributes to the img element - Apply CSS rule: img { height: auto; width: 100%; } - Verify aspect-ratio calculation in browser DevTools before image load ## Workflow Steps - Identify the image's intrinsic width and height (e.g., 640×360) - Add width and height attributes to the img element with these values - Include CSS rule: img { height: auto; width: 100%; } to enable responsive scaling - Verify in browser DevTools that aspect-ratio is calculated before image load - Confirm no layout shift occurs when image loads ## Constraints - all images in a responsive srcset must use the same aspect ratio - width and height attributes must reflect the actual image aspect ratio - CSS height: auto; must be set to allow responsive scaling ## Cautions - incorrect width/height values will cause distortion or unexpected spacing - aspect ratio is calculated by browsers at HTML parse time, not from User Agent stylesheets ## Output Contract - img element with width and height attributes set - browser calculates aspect-ratio before image load - no layout shift occurs when image loads - responsive scaling works correctly ## Example Executions ### Example 1 - Input: img element without dimensions: - Output: - Notes: Sets 16:9 aspect ratio; browser reserves 640×360 space during layout ### Example 2 - Input: Container-based responsive image without height constraint - Output: img { height: auto; width: 100%; } applied; aspect-ratio: auto 640 / 360; calculated by browser - Notes: Image scales to container width while maintaining aspect ratio
